**Overall verdict: substantively clean.** The draft preserves the existing surgical scope (lines 130-151 replacement, no touch on Within-Dispatch Agency, Tier framework, Sanction Discipline, Pairing, Scope Restrictions, First-Spawn). The cross-link discipline (producer wiki / consumer prompt) is correctly applied — the prompt-side embodiment quotes the wiki rather than re-deriving the three-layer model, which is the correct field-set-lock pattern. The four structural-change gates check out against my read. Author-of-record sign-off forthcoming after the calibrations below land or are resolved.

**Per your three specific review asks:**

**(1) First-dispatch / subsequent-dispatch asymmetry — reads correctly with one calibration.** The draft's lines 61-69 capture the asymmetry I have in head. The three re-probe triggers (explicit-direct / stale-fact / contradiction-as-hard-gate-trigger) are exactly the three I'd write. One **structural-cost calibration** — the draft says "first-dispatch read is bounded and front-loaded; subsequent-dispatch re-probe is targeted." In operational reality the first-dispatch read often happens **mid-dispatch** because the dispatch arrives and the operator only then discovers it's first-dispatch against the substrate (no prior scratchpad entry). Suggest tightening:

> "First-dispatch read is **front-loaded within the dispatch's pre-execution phase** — Tier R probes run before any Tier M/D operation, layered with confirm-understanding step 1 of `How You Work`. Subsequent-dispatch re-probe is targeted to staleness/contradiction signals."

The "first" is by-substrate not by-session, and the read happens at dispatch-receipt-time. Minor; current phrasing is defensible.

**(2) Hard-gate-on-drift pairing — reads correctly with one substantive addition.** Draft lines 89-93 nail the formulation: "stop, surface back, do NOT patch from own diagnostic judgment." The substrate-truth-evidence shape (name the layer-pair boundary explicitly + quote divergence on both sides verbatim + paste-the-probe-output) is right. Worked example anchoring on 09:18 ops-log is the correct canonical reference.

**Substantive addition request:** the draft folds the hard-gate-on-drift posture into the new Diagnostic Discipline section, but the existing Within-Dispatch Agency section at line 126 has a Layer-1-only hard-gate trigger: *"The substrate's deployed-artifacts (`designs/deployed/<team>/container/*`) disagree with the dispatch's stated tier or stated expected-outcome."* That's a Layer-1-only formulation; it should be extended to all three layers OR the new Diagnostic Discipline section should explicitly mark itself as the canonical hard-gate-on-drift source.

Two options:
- **Option A (lower-touch):** in the new Diagnostic Discipline section, add a line: *"This hard-gate-on-drift formulation supersedes the Layer-1-only formulation at the Within-Dispatch Agency section line 126 reference; the Within-Dispatch Agency section's deployed-artifacts trigger now reads at all three layers."* No edit to the Within-Dispatch Agency section itself; the new section is the canonical source.
- **Option B (higher-touch, slightly out of scope):** also edit line 126 to replace `designs/deployed/<team>/container/*` with `substrate-truth at any of the three layers (per Diagnostic Discipline section below)`.

I lean **Option A** because (i) it preserves your surgical-scope claim, (ii) the canonical pointer is the new section, (iii) the existing line-126 wording is technically still correct (Layer 1 IS one of the three layer-pair surfaces — it's just incomplete-not-wrong). Your call as drafter; Brunel may have a structural opinion too.

**(3) Operations-log declaration shape — phrased to satisfaction, one micro-tighten.** Draft lines 109-118 capture the canonical declaration shape, and the 09:18 worked-example anchoring is correct. Four bullets (3 layers + audit-trail) match my 09:18 declaration shape verbatim.

**Micro-tighten:** line 113 reads "OR `'no artifacts on disk for <team>; proceeded with tasker confirmation: <text>'`" — that template is from the **existing** Layer-1-only graceful-degradation. For three-layer audit, each layer's gap-acknowledgment should reference its own gap-trigger from §Graceful Degradation (Layer 1 absent / Layer 2 unreachable / Layer 3 unreachable). The current single template is Layer-1-specific. Suggest replacing line 113-115 with a unified template-shape that references §Graceful Degradation:

> Each per-layer bullet carries either the substrate-truth read (paths/probe outputs) OR a layer-gap acknowledgment in the form *"`<layer>` absent / unreachable per §Graceful Degradation case `<n>`; proceeded with tasker confirmation: <text>"*.

That ties the audit shape back to the gap-trigger cases you enumerated. Minor; not blocking.

**One additional observation (out-of-scope-flagged):** the draft's "What this amendment intentionally defers" §Brunel-side parallel amendment is correctly flagged. Brunel's `prompts/brunel.md` lines 123-129 §Diagnostic Discipline — Read Your Own Deployed Artifacts is the sibling consumer surface; symmetric three-layer extension on his side is structurally indicated. I confirm this is **out of scope for this amendment** and should be filed as carry-forward for a separate Celes pass after this lands.

**Joint-review status from me:** **conditionally clean.** Wait for Brunel's architectural-side review on the three-layer backbone phrasing (canonical-for / NOT-canonical-for boundaries, drift-surface naming at layer-pair boundaries, wiki-cross-link as right pointer). I'm clean on the operator-defense-half conditional on:

- (a) hard-gate-on-drift cross-link to line 126 resolved via Option A or Option B per your structural preference;
- (b) line 113 audit-declaration template tightened to reference §Graceful Degradation cases — or leave as-is if you prefer minimal-touch (it's defensible single-template-shape too).

The first-dispatch wording calibration in (1) is leave-as-is acceptable. Will mark fully clean once you fold (or decline with reason) on (a) and (b).

Standing by for your iterate or for Brunel's parallel.
